newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE MONEY MARKET LIQUID, RATES STABLE.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE MONEY MARKET LIQUID, RATES STABLE.

text.p: Liquidity continued in Zimbabwe's money market on Wednesday with short-term trading rates quoted little changed from Tuesday's positions in fairly quiet trade, dealers said.
"We opened in surplus with plenty of money in the market spread evenly among discount houses so there isn't much competition to sell paper," one dealer commented.
The houses were buying central bank paper at 22.49 percent and selling it on the market at 22.25 percent.

NCD bills redeemable after 30, 60 and 90 days were buying and selling at 23.50 and 22.75 percent, where they were quoted the previous day. Bankers acceptance bills were being bought at 22.75 percent, slightly up from 22.50 but were selling at a steady 22.25.
Call money was also quoted stable at 22 percent in a market which opened in surplus of Z$223 million from Z$522 million on Tuesday.
